changes: Add all five complete three-evaluation-seed results to an appendix table, with per-seed counts and mean/sample SD.
Distinguish fixed-task evaluation repeats from independent offline training seeds and explain deterministic zero SD.
Revise all 28 existing figure/table captions for experimental context, units, symbols and supported conclusions.
Replace generic Figure 3 commentary with an explanation of the five steps, persistent memory and three-replan goal weighting.

captions.label: fig:headline
captions.before: \textbf{Data augmentation and ECP provide complementary gains.} Success on 350 PushObj tasks per model at 150 controls. Frozen fixes an offline-pretrained ResNet world model; AdaJEPA updates that architecture online. Base data uses the released ResNet checkpoints or matched random-data LeWM training. Brackets show the total gain from base-data native planning to augmented ECP.
captions.after: \textbf{Data augmentation and ECP improve PushObj success.} Success (\%) on 350 tasks (50 per shape), with 150 controls and the original evaluation seed. Frozen fixes a pretrained ResNet; AdaJEPA updates it online. Base data uses released ResNet weights or random-data LeWM training; augmentation adds noisy contact interactions. Brackets show the combined gain in percentage points (pp).

captions.label: fig:teaser
captions.before: \textbf{Stalled execution is a signal for planning correction.} Eight views compare native failure and ECP success. Frozen holds the offline-pretrained ResNet world model fixed; AdaJEPA updates it online. Each center plot enlarges the boxed native trajectory over its labelled replan interval; $\Delta x,\Delta y$ are displacement from that interval's start, in pixels (px) or world units (u), with equal axis scales. Solid paths follow saved-action simulator replay, dots mark five-control intervals, and arrows show direction. In scene views, circles mark starts, stars agent goals, crosses failures, and diamonds successes; counts give terminating replans.
captions.after: \textbf{ECP resolves local stalls in four episodes.} Brown native paths fail; teal ECP paths succeed within 30 replans. Frozen fixes a pretrained ResNet; AdaJEPA updates it online. Center plots enlarge boxed intervals; $\Delta x,\Delta y$ are displacements in pixels (px) or world units (u). Dots mark five-control blocks. Circles/stars mark starts/goals, crosses/diamonds mark failure/success, and numbers count replans.

captions.label: fig:method
captions.before: \textbf{ECP connects execution feedback to planning.} Offline actions combine contact bias with Gaussian noise before collection. Step 3 illustrates PushObj, Maze, shifted PushT, and Rope execution. Step 4 detects small net movement relative to goal distance. Step 5 retains stagnation memory ($S$) and boosts goal weighting ($P$) for three calls, renewed by new triggers. The timeline highlights sustained correction inspired by ACT. Model parameters may remain fixed or adapt online.
captions.after: \textbf{How ECP uses execution feedback.} Offline, noisy contact-biased actions provide world-model training data. Steps 1--3 encode current/goal images, optimize predicted actions, and execute the first block. Step 4 detects small net movement relative to goal distance. Step 5 penalizes stalled-state revisits through persistent memory $S$ (blue), and boosts the unfinished proprioceptive goal term for three replans through $P$ (brown). New stalls renew the boost.

captions.label: tab:components
captions.before: \textbf{Component ablation on PushObj} ($\gamma_{\rm hi}=0.15$). Success (\%) on the same 350 tasks and 30-replan budget. $S$ denotes memory-based stagnation regularization; $P$ denotes temporary proprioceptive reweighting. Both checkpoints are offline-pretrained ResNet world models. Frozen fixes their parameters; AdaJEPA updates them online. Native omits ECP. Row maxima are bold.
captions.after: \textbf{ECP components improve PushObj success.} Success (\%) on 350 tasks, 30 replans, $\gamma_{\rm hi}=0.15$. $S/P$ denote stagnation memory/temporary proprioceptive reweighting. Released/Data aug. use published/interaction-biased pretrained ResNet checkpoints. Frozen fixes weights; AdaJEPA updates them online. Native disables ECP; bold marks row maxima.

captions.label: fig:threshold
captions.before: \textbf{Trigger-threshold sensitivity on PushObj.} AdaJEPA with the augmented-data ResNet, 350 tasks and 30 replans. ECP uses $S{+}P$ and $\gamma_{\rm lo}=\gamma_{\rm hi}/3$. Points show measured success; the dashed line is native planning.
captions.after: \textbf{Gains persist across stall thresholds.} AdaJEPA updates an augmented-data ResNet on 350 PushObj tasks with 30 replans. Teal points report ECP success (memory plus goal reweighting); dashed is native planning. Larger $\gamma_{\rm hi}$ detects stalls earlier; $\gamma_{\rm lo}=\gamma_{\rm hi}/3$.

captions.label: tab:timing
captions.before: \textbf{Triggered correction versus permanent reweighting and additional search} ($\gamma_{\rm hi}=0.15$). PushObj planning with the offline-pretrained, augmented-data ResNet world model held fixed. Permanent weighting uses the same $10\times$ multiplier as ECP. Rescue/harm counts are paired changes relative to native MPC.
captions.after: \textbf{Triggered correction preserves native successes.} Success (\%) on 350 PushObj tasks with a fixed, augmented-data ResNet and 30 replans. ECP uses memory $S$ and temporary goal reweighting $P$; permanent weighting always applies the $10\times$ boost. Lookahead tests extra action prefixes. Rescue/harm counts native failures recovered/successes lost.

captions.label: tab:maze
captions.before: \textbf{Stagnation memory on Maze.} Frozen holds the offline-pretrained ResNet world model fixed; AdaJEPA updates it online. Native omits ECP; Ours adds memory-only $S$. Success requires position error $<0.5$ on 100 tasks with a 30-replan budget.
captions.after: \textbf{Memory improves Maze success without regressions.} Success (\%) on 100 tasks within 30 replans, with 0.5-unit goal tolerance. Frozen fixes a pretrained ResNet; AdaJEPA updates it online. Native omits ECP; Ours adds memory $S$, after a prediction-loss plateau for AdaJEPA.

captions.label: tab:rope
captions.before: \textbf{Rope planning with DINO-WM.} Both methods keep the pretrained model fixed and predict/execute three pushes per plan. Ours uses fixed-strength $S$ after five warm-up pushes. Results cover 20 targets repeated under three seeds (60 runs per method). Success is CD $<0.3$. Pushes averages all runs, with a 20-push cap.
captions.after: \textbf{ECP improves Rope planning.} Fixed DINO-WM, three pushes per plan. Ours adds fixed-strength memory after five warm-up pushes. Twenty targets repeat under three seeds (60 runs). CD is mean final Chamfer distance; success requires CD $<0.3$. Pushes averages all runs, including failures capped at 20.

captions.label: fig:execution-recovery
captions.before: \textbf{Execution examples across four settings.} Brown and teal denote planning without and with ECP. Full-scene pairs show PushObj with ResNet (a--b), PushT with LeWM under red-agent/red-goal shifts (c--d), and Maze with AdaJEPA (e--f); labels report terminating replans. Rope pairs use DINO-WM with and without fixed-strength ECP, after twenty pushes in both (g) and (h); labels give final CD.
captions.after: \textbf{ECP recovers failed plans and reduces Rope error.} Brown/teal denote without/with ECP. In (a--f), labels give outcome and stopping replans (maximum 30). Rope pairs (g--h) show both methods after 20 pushes; CD is Chamfer distance (lower is better; success $<0.3$). ECP succeeds in (a--g) and lowers CD in (h), where both methods fail.

captions.label: tab:parameters
captions.before: \textbf{Implementation parameters.} The values describe the ResNet regularizer and the action-space instantiation of \cref{sec:action-space}. A disabled component uses $\kappa=0$ or $b=1$.
captions.after: \textbf{ECP settings for ResNet control.} Parameters apply to PushObj, PushT, and Maze; each replan executes five controls. The last row describes the alternative action-offset intervention. Setting $\kappa=0$ or $b=1$ disables memory or goal reweighting, respectively.

captions.label: tab:lewm-contact
captions.before: \textbf{LeWM controls.} The same offline-trained LeWM checkpoint is held fixed across 350 matched tasks; Native omits ECP.
captions.after: \textbf{Contact guidance gives the largest LeWM gain.} Success counts and percentages on 350 PushObj tasks with a fixed, augmented-data LeWM and 150 controls. Native has no correction. Other rows compare stall-triggered latent penalties, pusher weighting, physical action offsets, and contact costs; offsets are in pixels. Contact weight 10 performs best.

captions.label: tab:dinowm-aug
captions.before: \textbf{Interaction-biased augmentation transfers to DINO-WM.} PushObj success (\%) of DINO-WM with parameters fixed at test time and CEM on the same 350 tasks (50 per shape). Both models are trained for three epochs under a matched protocol that differs only in the action data.
captions.after: \textbf{Augmentation improves DINO-WM on every shape.} PushObj success (\%) on 50 tasks per shape, with fixed weights, CEM, and 150 controls. Both models train for three epochs, differing only in action data. Sq./sT mean square/small-T; Avg. averages seven shapes.

captions.label: tab:threshold
captions.before: \textbf{Trigger-threshold ablation on PushObj.} Augmented-data ResNet checkpoint with AdaJEPA online updates and $S{+}P$, 350 tasks, 30 replans, $\gamma_{\rm lo}=\gamma_{\rm hi}/3$. Triggered counts episodes with at least one detected stall; First is the median replan of the first trigger. Rescue/harm counts native failures recovered and native successes lost.
captions.after: \textbf{Earlier detection yields stable PushObj gains.} AdaJEPA with an augmented-data ResNet, memory and goal reweighting; 350 tasks, 30 replans, $\gamma_{\rm lo}=\gamma_{\rm hi}/3$. Triggered counts episodes with a stall; First is their median first-trigger replan. Rescue/harm counts native failures recovered/successes lost. All thresholds improve over native planning.

captions.label: tab:threshold-shape
captions.before: \textbf{Per-shape results of the trigger-threshold ablation.} PushObj success (\%) with the augmented-data checkpoint and $S{+}P$, 50 tasks per shape, 30 replans, and $\gamma_{\rm lo}=\gamma_{\rm hi}/3$. Frozen fixes the pretrained ResNet world model; AdaJEPA updates it online. Native omits ECP. Seen averages L, Z, $+$, and T; Unseen averages I, square (Sq.), and small-T (sT).
captions.after: \textbf{ECP gains across seen and unseen PushObj shapes.} Success (\%) on 50 tasks per shape with 30 replans. Frozen fixes an augmented-data ResNet; AdaJEPA updates it online. Native disables ECP; other rows use memory plus goal reweighting. Seen averages L, Z, $+$, T; Unseen averages I, square (Sq.), small-T (sT); All averages seven shapes. Frozen improves in both groups.

captions.label: tab:memory-strength
captions.before: \textbf{Memory strength and distance.} PushObj success (\%) with the augmented-data model and AdaJEPA. Proprioceptive reweighting is disabled; the native baseline is 74.9\%. All settings share the same trigger ($\gamma_{\rm hi}=0.15$) and $\beta=0.25$.
captions.after: \textbf{Joint latent memory outperforms proprioception-only memory.} PushObj success (\%) on 350 tasks with 30 replans and an augmented-data ResNet updated by AdaJEPA. $\kappa$ scales the memory penalty; Joint combines visual and proprioceptive distances. Goal reweighting is disabled; native success is 74.9\%.

captions.label: fig:push-distance
captions.before: \textbf{Completing a stalled PushObj trajectory.} Both controllers hold the offline-pretrained ResNet world model fixed. The curve reports joint pusher/object position error; lines mark the detected stall and the 20-pixel success threshold. The angle condition holds at the successful endpoint.
captions.after: \textbf{ECP completes a stalled PushObj episode.} Both runs use the same fixed, pretrained ResNet. Dashed/solid curves show native/ECP joint pusher--object position error in pixels. Vertical/horizontal lines mark stall detection and the 20-pixel success threshold. Only ECP crosses the threshold, at replan 17, with object-angle error also below $\pi/9$.

captions.label: tab:training
captions.before: \textbf{Augmented-data training across seeds.} Mean success percentage $\pm$ sample SD over three training seeds. Target streams and budgets are reported separately. Both use native planning without ECP and an offline-pretrained ResNet world model: Frozen fixes its weights; AdaJEPA updates them online.
captions.after: \textbf{Training-seed variability on PushObj.} Native-planning success (mean \% $\pm$ sample SD) over three augmented-data ResNet training seeds (0, 1, 2), without ECP. Frozen fixes weights; AdaJEPA updates them online. Rows evaluate 350 or 700 sampled targets with the indicated seeds and replan budgets. AdaJEPA improves both means.

captions.label: tab:action
captions.before: \textbf{Action-space instantiation with AdaJEPA.} Success (\%) at 30 replans on 350 tasks per stream. The variant uses a physical stall trigger, a bounded action offset, a temporary proprioceptive boost, and no latent memory. The streams share 35 target segments and are reported separately.
captions.after: \textbf{Physical action correction improves PushObj.} Success (\%) on 350 tasks per stream, with 30 replans and an augmented-data ResNet updated by AdaJEPA. Action offset combines a physical stall trigger, bounded pusher-goal offset, and temporary reweighting. Rescue/harm counts native failures recovered/successes lost. Streams share 35 target segments.

captions.label: tab:maze-full
captions.before: \textbf{Adaptive Maze results at shorter and longer execution budgets.} Successful tasks out of 100 at 20 and 50 replans; the 30-replan controls appear in \cref{tab:maze-controls}. Rescue/harm and the exact paired $p$ (\cref{sec:paired}) refer to the 50-replan comparison with AdaJEPA. All variants use AdaJEPA updates; the freeze controls stop adaptation without enabling either correction.
captions.after: \textbf{Memory complements continued adaptation on Maze.} Successes out of 100 tasks at 20/50 replans, using pretrained ResNet and AdaJEPA; goal tolerance is 0.5 units. $S/P$ denote memory/goal reweighting. Activation uses first stall, ten-replan delay, or prediction-loss plateau. Freeze stops updates without correction. Rescue/harm counts native failures recovered/successes lost at 50 replans; $p$ is the exact two-sided McNemar test against native AdaJEPA.

captions.label: tab:rope-ablation
captions.before: \textbf{Rope ablations with fixed DINO-WM weights.} $H$ is the predicted/executed pushes per plan; Warm is the number of warm-up pushes. Success requires CD $<0.3$, with a 20-push cap. Pushes averages all runs. The upper block pools three seeds on the same 20 targets; the horizon control below uses seed 99 only.
captions.after: \textbf{Fixed memory with warm-up performs best on Rope.} All rows use fixed DINO-WM. $S$ is memory with constant (Fixed) or severity-dependent (Dynamic) strength; $H$ is pushes predicted/executed per plan, Warm is pushes before detection. CD is mean final Chamfer distance; success requires CD $<0.3$. Pushes includes failures capped at 20. Seeds repeat the same 20 targets; the horizon control is separate.

captions.label: fig:rope-budget
captions.before: \textbf{Rope success versus executed pushes.} Each curve counts the fraction of 60 DINO-WM runs that have reached CD $<0.3$ by a given push budget (20 targets, three seeds). All variants predict and execute three pushes per plan, with success checked after each push. Warm-up counts pushes before stall detection begins.
captions.after: \textbf{Rope success versus push budget.} Percentage reaching Chamfer distance $<0.3$ by each push count: 20 targets repeated under three seeds, with fixed DINO-WM and three pushes per plan. $S$ is memory with fixed or severity-dependent strength; warm-up delays detection. Fixed $S$ with five warm-up pushes reaches the highest final success.

captions.label: fig:rope-rollouts
captions.before: \textbf{Matched Rope executions with DINO-WM.} Native planning (brown) and fixed-strength ECP with five warm-up pushes (teal), on two targets from seed 101. Columns align actual push counts. At push twenty, ECP succeeds in (a) and reaches lower CD in (b), where both runs remain above the 0.3 success threshold.
captions.after: \textbf{Rope trajectories at equal push counts.} Brown/teal denote native planning/fixed-strength ECP with five warm-up pushes, using the same fixed DINO-WM, start, and goal. Columns align executed pushes. CD is final Chamfer distance (lower is better; success $<0.3$). ECP succeeds in (a); in (b), it lowers CD but both runs fail.

captions.label: fig:diverse-execution
captions.before: \textbf{Recoveries across seven PushObj shapes and four Maze tasks.} Frozen fixes the offline-pretrained ResNet world model; AdaJEPA updates it online. Pairs share a 30-replan budget. Solid paths follow verified simulator replay; dots mark five-control intervals and stars mark agent goals. These selected cases illustrate behavior; aggregate results use complete task lists.
captions.after: \textbf{Recoveries across seven PushObj shapes and four Maze tasks.} Paired brown native paths fail and teal ECP paths succeed from shared starts/goals within 30 replans. Frozen fixes a pretrained ResNet; AdaJEPA updates it online. Dots mark five-control blocks. These selected episodes show ECP escaping repeated local paths.

captions.label: fig:pusht-rollouts
captions.before: \textbf{Recorded PushT executions under visual shifts with LeWM.} Brown and teal identify planning without and with ECP, with all model weights fixed. Labels count executed controls; final frames are actual stopping states. ECP succeeds under both color shifts while native planning exhausts its budget. The goal column gives the target observation, not a predicted image.
captions.after: \textbf{ECP recovers PushT under color shifts.} Paired runs use the same fixed LeWM, start, goal, and 150-control budget. Brown/teal label planning without/with ECP; frame numbers count executed controls. ECP succeeds under both red-agent and red-goal shifts, while native planning exhausts its budget. The right column shows the goal observation.

captions.label: tab:maze-controls
captions.before: \textbf{Correction type and schedule on Maze.} Success (\%) on 100 tasks at 30 replans with the released, offline-pretrained ResNet world model. Frozen fixes its parameters; AdaJEPA updates them online; the two freeze controls disable both $S$ and $P$. Rescue/harm is relative to native planning with the same update rule.
captions.after: \textbf{Correction type and timing determine Maze recovery.} Success (\%) on 100 tasks with 30 replans. Frozen fixes a pretrained ResNet; AdaJEPA updates it online. $S/P$ denote memory/goal reweighting. Activation uses the first stall, a ten-replan delay, or a prediction-loss plateau. Freeze stops updates without correction. Rescue/harm counts native failures recovered/successes lost; loss-gated $S$ avoids losses.

captions.label: tab:main
captions.before: \textbf{Comparison with recent world-model controllers on PushObj and PushT.} Success (\%) at 150 controls; bold marks column maxima. Frozen fixes an offline-pretrained ResNet world model; AdaJEPA updates it online. Released denotes the published checkpoint. PushObj uses 50 tasks per shape; DINO-WM and LeWM use one archived task list; Frozen, AdaJEPA, and Ours use a second list over the same shapes. Sq., sT, and S\&P denote square, small-T, and salt-and-pepper noise. Avg. covers seven shapes or six visual shifts. Agent, Object, and Goal denote red-color shifts. Ours uses augmented data with $\gamma_{\rm hi}=0.45$ on PushObj and $0.15$ on PushT.
captions.after: \textbf{World-model control on PushObj and PushT.} Success (\%) within 150 controls; bold marks column maxima. Each shape/condition uses 50 tasks. Avg. covers seven shapes or six shifts, excluding Clean. Sq., sT, S\&P mean square, small-T, salt-and-pepper noise; Agent/Object/Goal recolor that component red. Frozen fixes a pretrained ResNet; AdaJEPA updates it online. Released uses published weights; Ours adds augmented training and ECP, with AdaJEPA achieving the highest means. PushObj task lists differ between DINO-WM/LeWM and ResNet controllers.

captions.label: tab:pusht-ecp
captions.before: \textbf{Checkpoint and intervention comparisons on PushT.} Success (\%) on the same 50 tasks and at most 30 replans. Both checkpoints are offline-pretrained ResNet world models: Frozen fixes parameters, while AdaJEPA updates them online. Released uses the published weights; Data aug. uses interaction-biased training. Paired ECP on/off runs share tasks and the pre-trigger random stream. Avg. covers six shifts.
captions.after: \textbf{ECP improves PushT across checkpoints and shifts.} Success (\%) on 50 matched tasks per condition, with 30 replans of five controls. Released/Data aug. use published/interaction-biased pretrained ResNet checkpoints. Frozen fixes weights; AdaJEPA updates them online. S\&P is salt-and-pepper noise; Red columns recolor the named component. Avg. excludes Clean. ECP matches or improves native success in every column.

captions.label: tab:eval-seeds
captions.after: \textbf{Headline results across three evaluation seeds.} Each seed repeats 350 fixed PushObj tasks per model, with unchanged checkpoints and 150 controls. Seed columns count successes; the final column gives mean success (\%) $\pm$ sample SD. Seeds are 100/200/300 for ResNet and 2000/2001/2002 for LeWM. Frozen/LeWM keep pretrained weights fixed; AdaJEPA updates ResNet online. Augmented data adds noisy contact interactions. Zero SD reflects deterministic evaluation; ECP improves AdaJEPA in every seed.

captions.label: tab:extra-baselines
captions.before: \textbf{Additional representation controls on PushT.} Success (\%) $\uparrow$ on the same 50 targets per shift, using CEM and a 150-control budget. All model weights are fixed at test time. Averages cover all six shifts.
captions.after: \textbf{Representation baselines on shifted PushT.} Success (\%) on 50 matched tasks per condition, with fixed weights, CEM, and 150 controls. S\&P denotes salt-and-pepper noise; Agent/Object/Goal recolor that component red. Avg. covers six shifts. DDP-WM has the highest mean among these baselines.
